summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman was admitted with fevers and toe pain. She had recently been treated for cellulitis but developed persistent fever and diarrhea. Workup revealed MSSA bacteremia, likely originating from her left chest port. The port was removed, and she was started on IV vancomycin, later transitioned to nafcillin. A PICC line was placed for outpatient antibiotic administration. Blood cultures cleared, and she remained stable with no cardiac involvement on echocardiogram. Diarrhea was non-infectious and managed supportively. She was discharged to an extended care facility to complete a two-week course of IV nafcillin, with plans for PICC removal upon completion.
problems: Local infection due to central venous catheter, initial encounter
